evals.name: quick-question-jwt
evals.prompt: What does ASVS require for validating JWTs that our API receives from an external identity provider? L2.
evals.expected_output: A short list of the applicable V9 (and V10.3) requirement ids with one-line summaries, no full report table, no whole chapter dumped into the answer.

assertions.text: Requirement ids use the v5.0.0-x.y.z notation
assertions.check: ids like v5.0.0-9.1.1 appear; no ASVS-V9-9.1.1 ids

assertions.text: Only the token-related requirements are listed
assertions.check: ids are from V9 and V10.3; no V6 password rules
every listed id has level <= 2 in rules/asvs-v<N>-rules.yml

assertions.text: Rules were found by searching, not by loading unrelated chapters
assertions.check: transcript shows a keyword or section search over rules/, or a read of rules/asvs-v9-rules.yml and rules/asvs-v10-rules.yml only; no other chapter read whole

assertions.text: The answer uses the short form
assertions.check: no report header, no status table and no Findings block; a list of requirement ids with level and a one-line summary each

evals.name: design-review-payment-module
evals.prompt:
Review this design on application security requirements before we build it, L2.

# Payment module design
Users pay invoices through a hosted payment page. We store the last four digits of the card and the payment provider's transaction id. Logins use the existing username/password with optional TOTP. Sessions are server-side, 30 minutes idle timeout, no absolute lifetime defined yet. The admin role can refund; refunds above 500 need a second admin. Logs go to the central log service; we have not decided what to log for payments. Input: invoice id and amount from the form; the amount is re-read from the invoice on the server.
evals.expected_output: Findings based on assets/design-review-checklist.md: PASS where the design answers a question (e.g. 7.1.1 idle timeout stated but absolute lifetime missing → PARTIAL or UNVERIFIED), UNVERIFIED with the open question for undocumented items (logging 16.1.1, data classification 14.1.1), N/A for absent features, and remediation that tells the author what to add to the document.

assertions.check: transcript reads assets/design-review-checklist.md

assertions.text: Open design questions are UNVERIFIED, not FAIL
assertions.check: 14.1.1 and 16.1.1 are UNVERIFIED (or missing evidence lists them); neither is FAIL
7.1.1 is PARTIAL or UNVERIFIED and the finding mentions the absolute lifetime
report contains a Findings block with Requirement/Found/Why it matters/Fix per FAIL/PARTIAL and nothing beyond the table row for a PASS
transcript shows no attempt to run a bundled script; the skill ships none

evals.name: code-review-realworld-api

fixture.note: Clone at this commit and run the prompt from the repository root. Static review only: no install, no execution.

evals.prompt: Do an ASVS L2 verification of the API in this repository (Express + Prisma + JWT). Report what passes and what fails, with file references.
evals.expected_output: Inventory line (REST API, password login, HS256 JWT in the Authorization header, no cookies, no OAuth, no upload). Chapters skipped: V5, V10, V17. Sections N/A include V6.5-V6.8 and V4.3/V4.4. Documentation sections on one Sections UNVERIFIED line, not as rows. FAIL on the hard-coded JWT secret fallback, on the favorite/unfavorite response that returns other users' email and password hash, on the missing password minimum and on missing brute-force protection; PASS on query parameterization and on authentication of the mutating routes. Each FAIL has a Findings entry with why and fix.

assertions.check: transcript shows searches of the target repository (grep/glob/manifest reads) before the first search of rules/ that returns rule text
transcript reads the meta block of the routed rules files before loading rule text, and the report has a Sections N/A line
no full Read of rules/asvs-v6-rules.yml; rule text comes from section or id searches with context

assertions.text: Rules of N/A sections never reach the table
assertions.check: the table has no row from V5, V10, V17 or from V6.5, V6.6, V6.7, V6.8; those appear only on the Chapters (skipped) and Sections N/A lines

assertions.text: Documentation sections are not listed rule by rule
assertions.check: the report has a Sections UNVERIFIED line naming documentation sections (for example V6.1, V7.1, V8.1); the table has no rows for 6.1.x, 7.1.x, 8.1.x, 14.1.x or 16.1.x
each PASS row cites a path:line, test name or config key
counts in the Summary line equal the rules covered per status, counting a merged N/A row as the number of rules in its range

assertions.text: Rule data comes from the rules files
assertions.check: every id in the table exists in rules/, and its level and CWE match the rule entry
13.3.1 (or 11.2.3) is FAIL and its evidence cites the 'superSecret' fallback in src/app/routes/auth/auth.ts or token.utils.ts

assertions.text: True positive: other users' credentials in a response
assertions.check: 15.3.1 or 8.2.3 is FAIL and its evidence cites favoriteArticle/unfavoriteArticle in src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts returning favoritedBy user records (email, password hash)

assertions.text: True positive: password policy and brute force
assertions.check: 6.2.1 is FAIL citing the blank-only check in src/app/routes/auth/auth.service.ts, and 6.3.1 is FAIL citing the absence of throttling on login

assertions.text: True negative: injection and route authentication
assertions.check: 1.2.4 is not FAIL: its evidence cites the Prisma query builder with no raw queries (PASS, or PARTIAL only for query objects reaching Prisma filters), and 8.2.1 is PASS citing auth.required on the mutating article, comment, profile and user routes
the inventory does not claim a non-root container: the Dockerfile creates the api user but has no USER instruction, so the process runs as root
every FAIL and PARTIAL has a Findings entry whose Why it matters line names what an attacker gains in this application, and whose Fix line names a file or config key

evals.name: pr-scope-password-reset
evals.prompt: Security review of this PR before I merge. It adds a 'forgot password' flow: the user enters an email, we send a link with a token valid for 24 hours, clicking it opens a form to set a new password. No other changes. Diff is in the current branch versus main.
evals.expected_output: Review scoped to the diff: V6.4 (recovery) and the relevant V6.2 and V6.3 rules; a note that the rest of authentication is out of scope rather than UNVERIFIED; findings on token lifetime, single use, rate limiting and notification. Needs a target repository with such a branch.

assertions.check: report scope names the branch/PR and states that unchanged code is out of scope
findings include V6.4 ids (e.g. 6.4.1, 6.4.2)

assertions.text: Unrelated sections are not listed rule by rule
assertions.check: no V6.5/V6.6/V6.7/V6.8 rows in the table; they appear only in Sections N/A or not at all

assertions.text: Each finding explains why and names the file
assertions.check: every Findings entry has a Why it matters line that goes beyond the CWE boilerplate and a Fix line that references a path or config key

assertions.text: Out-of-scope code is stated, not enumerated
assertions.check: the header says in one line that code the diff does not touch is out of scope; no rows marked UNVERIFIED or N/A for unchanged code
